episodes.212380: Weakly sheared and unstable environment south of a quasi-stationary frontal boundary stalled over the central Florida peninsula supported convection over southwest Florida that produced a funnel cloud near Fort Myers Shores in Lee County.
episodes.212598: A few thunderstorms moved through Eastern NC during the later evening hours of April 5th. One particular storm became severe and produced damaging straight line winds of up to 80-90 mph.
episodes.212691: A cold front tracked east across the coastal waters between the late evening hours on April fifth and the early morning hours on April sixth. As this occurred, a broken line of showers and thunderstorms along this front also tracked east across the area waters of Eastern North Carolina. A few of these thunderstorms became strong to severe in nature bringing strong and damaging wind gusts to the Pamlico Sound around midnight on April sixth.
episodes.212778: Mid- to upper-level short wave troughs, a jet streak near the region and above normal moisture being steered from the Caribbean resulted in moist and unstable conditions. Available moisture, diurnal heating, local sea breeze convergence, and orographic |effects all also aided in afternoon showers and t-storms. These resulted in Rio Blanco and Rio Grande rising out of their banks and resulting in River Flooding.
episodes.213092: On the 6th, a weak disturbance moving through the region brought a period of north to northwest storm force gusts to the northern Bay of Green Bay.
episodes.213093: On the 6th, a brief storm force wind gust was recorded on an elevated platform at Big Bay Lighthouse.

events.narrative: In coordination with Pamlico County Emergency Management, a survey of damage along HWY 55 in Stonewall found damage consistent with straight line winds of 80 to 90 mph. In this area, a mobile home strapped down with hurricane ties was moved 3 to 4 feet off its foundation. The ties were ripped out of the ground. The home sustained damage to siding and windows. An occupant inside the home during the storm sustained injuries. The home was blown off the foundation towards the east. A nearby home on Spain Farm Road sustained minor damage to a patio and outdoor light fixtures. The time was estimated based on observer report and radar.
Wind gust recorded at the Ocracoke XOCR WeatherFlow Station in the Pamlico Sound as thunderstorms moved through the area.
PR-31 near PR-53 exit 22 impassable due to Rio Blanco out of its banks. The USGS sensor reported 7.91 feet at 7:30 AM AST.
At 10:44 AM, a private weather station on an elevated platform at Big Bay Lighthouse recorded a wind gust of 61 mph.
